title: Billing export runbook: edge cases & alert mapping
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook for billing exports and related cost-allocation UX. Focus: make export behavior predictable for customers, define handling for edge cases (partial invoices, multi-currency consolidation, tag collisions), and map budget/alert semantics to export rows. This doc is intentionally practical — wireframe notes followed by decision rules and a prioritized backlog of follow-ups.

Background/context:
- Multiple customers reported divergent CSVs across repeated exports when invoices were reprocessed (refunds/adjustments).
- Support tickets show confusion about which line items are considered "billable" vs "adjustment" and how they map to cost centers.
- Product goal: reduce support friction by providing a clear, auditable export format and by surface-level UI affordances for alerts and budget attribution.

User personas:
- Finance lead at mid-market SaaS (Primary): needs monthly reconciliable CSVs, consistent row IDs, timezone-agnostic date fields, and clear currency columns.
- Platform engineer (Secondary): wants API-first exports (scheduled webhook/curl) and incremental export for automation.
- PM/Engineering manager (Tertiary): wants quick filtered views in console and ability to download subset for audits.

Wireframe / modal copy (export flow):
- Export modal header: "Export billing data"
- Subheader: "Generate a CSV with usage, pricing, and allocation metadata. Exports are snapshot-based and idempotent."
- Controls:
  - Date range: [start date] — [end date] (UTC default, tooltip: "Exports are generated in UTC; invoice dates use invoice timezone where applicable")
  - Granularity: [Line items | Daily aggregates | Monthly invoice] (help text: "Line items ~= per-request/usage; Daily aggregates are rolled up by date")
  - Include adjustments: [checkbox] (default: checked)
  - Cost center mapping: [All | tag:key=value | manual CSV mapping upload]
  - Output format: [CSV | Parquet]
  - Delivery: [Download now | Schedule | Webhook URL]
  - Filename pattern preview: "redwood-billing-{{org}}-{{start}}_{{end}}-{{export-id}}.csv"
- Confirm CTA: "Generate export" ; Secondary CTA: "Save schedule"

Export schema (recommended CSV column set) — canonical order used for wireframes and API docs (keep stable):
- export_id, export_timestamp_utc, row_id, invoice_id, invoice_date_utc, usage_start_utc, usage_end_utc, resource_id, model_name, model_variant, tokens_consumed, quantity, unit_price, net_amount, adjustment_amount, currency, cost_center, allocation_tags, billing_account_id, region, zone, provider_instance_id, note, reconciled_flag, reconciliation_id

Key decisions and rules (to include in the export engine):
1) Row identity & idempotency:
   - row_id must be globally unique and persistent for the life of the invoice. If line is adjusted later (refund/credit), a new row is created with a new row_id and the original row_id preserved via 'reconciliation_id' pointing to the original.
   - export_id + row_id => deterministic row in a given snapshot. Re-running the same export_id should return identical CSV.
2) Adjustments and refunds:
   - Always include adjustments unless user explicitly unchecks. Adjustment rows have negative net_amount and adjustment_amount fields populated; also include 'note' with reason (e.g., "refund for duplicate charges").
3) Currency handling:
   - Exports contain a 'currency' column (currency of charge). Provide optional 'fx_converted_net_amount' and 'fx_base_currency' when org selects a base currency in settings. Document FX date and rate source (end of invoice day, Bank-of-X feed).
4) Cost center mapping and tag collisions:
   - Priority: explicit CSV mapping uploaded by customer > cost-center tag on resource > default org bucket. If multiple tags present, use the highest priority tag based on configured tag precedence order (exposed in UI). If collision unresolved, mark 'cost_center' as "ambiguous:{tags}" and surface in alerts.
5) Timezones and date fields:
   - All timestamp columns in export are UTC. 'invoice_date_utc' derived from invoice timezone normalized to UTC. Keep a separate 'original_invoice_timezone' column if needed in future.
6) Partial invoices and mid-period adjustments:
   - If an invoice is adjusted after a scheduled export window, exports should not mutate prior export_ids. New exports include both original rows and new adjustment rows with reconciliation_id linking them.
7) Sampling and performance tradeoffs for huge orgs:
   - For orgs with >10M rows in date range, we support streaming Parquet and incremental export tokens (cursor + resume). UI should display row estimate and warn: "Large export — use scheduled webhook or Parquet for performance."
8) PII and redaction:
   - Default export redacts user-email and IP fields. Provide a settings toggle for "include raw resource labels" with warning.

Alert & Budgets mapping notes (console UX):
- Budget types: monthly spend, forecasted monthly burn, model-specific spend, project/tag-based spend.
- UI: budgets are defined against the same dimensions as exports (currency, time window, cost_center/tags).
- Alert types and suggested severity mapping for wireframes:
  - INFO: forecast crossed 50% of budget (email only)
  - WARNING: forecast crossed 75% (email + Slack webhook)
  - CRITICAL: forecast crossed 95% or actual spend exceeds budget (email + Slack + console banner + optional PagerDuty)
- Alert content for CSV export rows: when an alert is triggered, we attach a short 'alert_event_id' to relevant export rows in subsequent scheduled exports for traceability. Also include 'budget_rule_id' column when exporter scoped to a budget.

Edge cases observed in Support tickets (concrete examples):
- Customer A: exported CSV for Aug 1-31 on Sep 5; on Sep 10 a credit memo posted and reprocessing changed invoice totals — customer re-ran export and couldn't reconcile old and new rows.
  - Proposed UX: exports are snapshoted per-export_id. Add a visible timeline on export history with "snapshot time" and link to reconciliation diff helper.
- Customer B: tags used for cost centers changed mid-month; earlier usage rows now map to a different cost_center in subsequent exports.
  - Proposed: export uses tag state at time of usage (store tag mapping snapshot). In UI, surface "tag assignment at usage time" toggle.
- Customer C: multiple currencies in single invoice (rare) — downstream accounting wants base-currency column.
  - Proposed: include fx_converted_net_amount and a 'fx_rate' and 'fx_rate_date' column whenever multiple currencies are present.

Backlog / action items (prioritized):
1) P0: Implement stable export schema and export_id snapshoting. Backend ticket: JIRA-BILL-78 (owner: Arjun).
2) P0: Export modal wireframe + copy iteration — usability testing with 3 finance customers. (Owner: Maya)
3) P1: Parquet streaming support + resume tokens (performance for large orgs).
4) P1: Tag snapshotting at usage time + UI toggle for historical vs current tag mapping.
5) P2: FX conversion columns and admin setting for base currency.
6) P2: Add reconciliation diff helper (UX: side-by-side CSV diff with filters).

Unresolved questions/discussion points (notes to self):
- How large should the export retention be for downloads in console (30 days? 90 days?) — compliance wants 7 years of audit data but we cannot host huge CSVs indefinitely. Possible compromise: store only snapshot metadata and a link to archived Parquet in long-term object store.
- Should we attempt deterministic stable 'row_id' for legacy invoices, or create reconciliation mapping for all historical exports? This impacts engineering complexity.
- What is the canonical source for FX rates? Bank-of-X vs internal daily mid-market. Need legal sign-off for financial reporting.

Microcopy and small UX bits to include in wireframes:
- Export success toast: "Export queued — you'll receive a download link when ready. Exports are immutable snapshots."
- Error: "Export failed — please check date range or contact billing-support@redwood.ai"
- Schedule cadence choices: Daily, Weekly (Mon), Monthly (1st), Quarterly, Custom cron.
- When scheduling webhook: "We will POST a JSON manifest with signed URL to your endpoint."

Short checklist for QA and support docs (to add to Support KB):
- Repro steps to verify idempotent export behavior
- How to interpret reconciliation rows and diff helper export
- How to filter exported CSV for cost_center and tag ambiguities
- Known limitations: historical tag reassignment, max export row estimate in UI

Notes and quick references (scratch):
- Related tickets: JIRA-BILL-78, JIRA-BILL-101 (parquet streaming), CONFLUENCE-12345 (billing schema draft)
- Slack threads: #billing-exports (links in linked_artifacts)

Status: draft — please add product review comments inline. Intend to move to in_review after PM + engineering alignment and a quick legal check around FX source by 2025-11-20.

---
Notes to self (very rough):
- Consider adding a small "export diff" endpoint in API to fetch only reconciliation changes between export_ids for automation consumers.
- UX prototype: add a small "View snapshot" link next to each scheduled export row in the console that shows export metadata and row counts.
